newsitem.title: USA: Dana Corp looks to new ventures for growth.
newsitem.headline: Dana Corp looks to new ventures for growth.

text.p: Dana Corp said Monday it plans to aggressively sharpen its focus on its eight core businesses and add technology and product depth in light of its record first quarter earnings of $92.6 million, largely through a group of new ventures that it expects to help increase shareholder value.
"Our first quarter results lay a strong foundation for the year," said Dana Chairman Southwood J. Morcott. "At the close of 1996, we outlined our 'Beyond 2000' strategy for growth.

"By completing the two largest acquisitions and the largest divestiture in Dana history during the first quarter, we've made a strong statement about our commitment to growth, profitability and increased shareholder value."

The company said the February acquisition of the assets of the worldwide piston ring and cylinder liner operations of SPX Corp for $223 million provides it with important new customer relationships around the world and has spurred it to elevate its Engine Products Group to core business status.
The company is also looking to other new ventures to boost its prospects.

Among them are the formation of a joint venture company with Przedsiebiorstwu FILTRON in Gostyn, Poland; construction later this year of a truck frame manufacturing facility in Owensboro, Ky.; and a contract with Compaq Computer Corp for its commercial credit unit to provide Compaq-branded, turnkey microcomputer lease financing to the growing small and medium business market in the U.S. and Canada.
